units.text: INT. VICTORIAN TELEGRAPH OFFICE - NIGHT
Gaslight hisses.
Brass keys.
A wall of pigeonholes and paper tape curling like ivy.
The air smells of lamp oil and wet wool.
A grandfather clock ticks toward midnight.
ELIZABETH HARGROVE-WYNNE, 30s, in a gray wool dress with high collar, sits at the main key, fingers dancing.
A pince-nez is perched on her nose.
Her supervisor, MR. THADDEUS OSGOOD, 60s, a bald man with muttonchops, hovers over her shoulder.
A messenger boy, PERCIVAL "PERCY" TWEEDLE, 12, dozes on a stool.
A cleaner, MRS. KEZIAH AMADI, 50s, mops the floor with deliberate slowness.
On a bench, CAPTAIN RUPERT BELLAMY, 40s, a naval officer with a bandaged hand, waits with his cap on his knee.
The key clatters.
Elizabeth jots a line.
She stops, rereads it, and slides it to Osgood.
Mr. Osgood. This came from Calais.
units.name: ELIZABETH

units.text: Good Lord.
units.name: OSGOOD

units.text: What is it?
units.name: CAPTAIN BELLAMY

units.text: Nothing, sir. A routine dispatch.
units.name: OSGOOD

units.text: It is not routine.
units.name: ELIZABETH

units.text: Miss Hargrove-Wynne.
units.name: OSGOOD

units.text: It names the Admiralty. It says the Channel fleet has been sold.
units.name: ELIZABETH

units.text: Percy wakes, rubs his eyes.
Mrs. Amadi stops mopping.
Bellamy rises, face pale.
Sold? To whom?
units.name: CAPTAIN BELLAMY

units.text: It does not say.
units.name: ELIZABETH

units.text: It is a forgery.
units.name: OSGOOD

units.text: It came on the Admiralty cipher.
units.name: ELIZABETH

units.text: Then it is a very good forgery.
units.name: OSGOOD

units.text: The door bangs open.
A tall man in evening dress enters, shaking rain from his coat: SIR ALARIC FENWICK-ROTH, 50s, an MP, with silver hair and a gold-topped cane.
He sweeps off his hat.
Mr. Osgood. I understand there has been a message.
units.name: SIR ALARIC

units.text: Sir Alaric. We were just discussing it.
units.name: OSGOOD

units.text: Then let us discuss it privately.
units.name: SIR ALARIC

units.text: He extends a gloved hand.
Osgood hesitates, glances at Elizabeth, then slowly hands over the slip.
Sir Alaric reads, folds it, and tucks it inside his coat.
Miss, you have not seen this.
units.name: SIR ALARIC

units.text: I have seen it, sir. I transcribed it.
units.name: ELIZABETH

units.text: Then you will un-transcribe it.
units.name: SIR ALARIC

units.text: Percy sneaks a look at Mrs. Amadi.
She raises one eyebrow.
Bellamy puts on his cap and steps forward.
Sir Alaric, I would like to see that dispatch.
units.name: CAPTAIN BELLAMY

units.text: Captain, I am afraid it concerns matters above your station.
units.name: SIR ALARIC

units.text: My ship is in that fleet.
units.name: CAPTAIN BELLAMY

units.text: A beat.
Sir Alaric studies him, then smiles thinly and removes the slip.
So it is.
units.name: SIR ALARIC

units.text: He hands it over.
Bellamy reads.
His jaw tightens.
He looks at Elizabeth.
Miss Hargrove-Wynne. I should like to send a reply.
units.name: CAPTAIN BELLAMY

units.text: To Calais?
units.name: ELIZABETH

units.text: To everyone.
units.name: CAPTAIN BELLAMY

units.text: She turns to the key.
The clock begins to strike midnight.
